description: Version 2 orders, one case per mode and pool. Items are in the version 1 key-order shape (id, kind, optional seriesId, premiere, year, season, episode). caps is {series, film} as the scheduler reads it (defaults already filled in); films maps a film ID to its collection ID, already resolved (only films of collections named in sources, a film in several under the smallest collection ID); an item not in films is not in a collection. rotation: groups are a series' episodes (group ID the series ID, in-group key of randomInOrder, cap caps.series), a collection's films (group ID the collection ID, release order: undated flag, date, ID; cap caps.film) and every other item alone (cap 1); group key = splitmix64(seed + fnv1a64(groupIdBytes)) with the channel seed, ascending unsigned, ties by group ID bytes; walk in rounds, each group's turn takes up to its cap of next items; groups lists them in key order with key, cap and itemIds; one turn is one run, blockLength is not read. A rotation case whose items carry runtimeMs (a decimal string of milliseconds) also gives epochHours (24): a turn stops before the item that would make the sum of its runtimes longer than epochHours * 3600000 (a turn always holds at least one item), and the group's next turn continues from that item; in a rotation case without runtimeMs no turn comes near that limit. capped shuffle (mode shuffle with caps): shuffleOrder is the version 1 shuffle with seedN (seedN = splitmix64(seed + n * gamma)), keys its keys; groups (sorted by group ID) gives each group's cap and items in shuffle order; walk lists every step's N (items left before the step), the tight group or null, the picked group and the item; order is the capped order and runs cut it into blockLength runs from the first item. inOrder: series groups (in-group key) and every other item, every film included, alone; groups in the order of (undated flag, date of the group's first dated item in its own order, group ID bytes), with undated 0 or 1 and date or null; runs of blockLength.
source: Computed with an independent Python reference written from docs/rules-format.md only (version 1 and version 2: Groups in version 2, rotation, the capped shuffle, inOrder, Filters, Building the schedule, Primitives), without reading any Kotlin. The reference script is not committed, as for the version 1 vectors; it reproduces every case of key-order.json and lineup.json. Item IDs are synthetic.

vectors.name: rotation long turn, a turn stops at the first item that does not fit, even when a later one would
vectors.note: E1 is 20 h; E2 (5 h) would make 25 h, so the turn is [E1]. The next turn takes E2 E3 (6 h); E4 (22 h) would make 28 h, so it waits for the turn after. A turn never skips an item to take a later, shorter one.
